title: Wolstenholme's Theorem OQ-02-OQ-02: Mod p³ and Wolstenholme Primes
description: Proves Wolstenholme's theorem (1862): C(2p-1,p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p³) for prime p ≥ 5. Strategy: power sum vanishing via cyclic group generator + Vandermonde identity. Defines Wolstenholme primes (mod p⁴ condition) and states the open question: does any Wolstenholme prime exist with p ≡ 1 (mod 4)? 1 axiom for the Vandermonde reduction. 14 theorems.

overview.historicalContext: Wolstenholme (1862) proved C(2p-1,p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p³). Strengthens Babbage's mod p² result.
overview.problemStatement: Prove Wolstenholme's theorem via power sum vanishing.
overview.proofStrategy: Sum units power vanishing: pick generator g, reindex x ↦ gx to show sum = 0 when (p-1) ∤ m; combine with Vandermonde to get mod p³.
keyInsights: **wolstenholme_mod_p3**: Wolstenholme's theorem: the central binomial coefficient satisfies a strong congruence mod p³
